speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I need to evaluate your postpartum fever and abdominal tenderness to determine the cause. How many days postpartum are you, and how high has your temperature reached?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. The combination of uterine tenderness, fever, and decreased bowel sounds after a prolonged labor is concerning for complications like uterine infection or an abdominal abscess. Have you experienced any foul-smelling vaginal discharge or chills?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of uterine tenderness, fever, and foul-smelling discharge (if present) strongly suggests a uterine infection. Given the added symptoms of decreased bowel sounds and urinary frequency, we need to rule out an abdominal abscess or urinary tract involvement. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC), Urinalysis, and C-Reactive Protein (CRP). Please let me know if you have noticed any foul odor from your vaginal discharge or if you are experiencing chills.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum endometritis with urinary tract involvement.
